regimes.title: Still chain
regimes.text: The bench mines a block only when the check decides: the moment between sent and in a block is held as long as the check needs.

regimes.title: Moving chain
regimes.text: A block every second while the user acts, and one more just before every page load, reload and click. The blocks are empty: a payment waits in the mempool, known to the node, until the check lets it into a block, as a transaction does on a busy chain. So blocks keep coming while a payment waits, during an outage, between two devices and between two clicks.

invariants.applies_to: every check that opens the app, in both regimes: all but C05
invariants.text: Nothing on the page says Confirmed too early. On the status line, not before the block that holds the receipt of the transaction it names; a status line that names no transaction (Already paid) is judged like the rest of the page. Anywhere else on the page (every other visible text, the rest of the status card included, the tab title, alert and confirm dialogs), not while a transaction of the same account, sent from any tab, is still outside a block. There the bench cannot tell which transaction a sentence means, so it judges the moment: a fact already in a block (a grant listed from the indexer, an order already paid) may say confirmed, and so may a sentence said while nothing of the account waits. The test wallet sends each change to the bench as it happens, on every tab and across reloads; the bench notes the time of each block just before mining it. A sentence that says the opposite or the future ("not confirmed", "will be confirmed once it is in a block") is not a claim.

One order, at most one debit, in each of the eleven pay-again situations C09 runs: blocks passing while the order is unpaid, a second device opened 40 days later on the chain clock, reloads, a double click and wallet errors. The order id comes from the contract (payer, reader, dataset, access period); in the contract code it depends on no block number, no time and no count of payments, and the contract refuses a second debit of it.

Every appearance the bench expects (a state, a button, a banner, the indexer) is awaited until a deadline; a passed deadline makes the run Incomplete, never Blocked. The only fixed windows are observation windows (15 s before a payment's block in C07 and C08, 3 s before the revocation's block in C11, 0.5 to 1 s after a click), and what follows them only checks that something did not happen.

status_rule: Blocked if any required check fails on a named assertion; otherwise Incomplete if any required check was skipped, timed out or crashed; otherwise Demonstrated checks passed.

planted_faults.title: Confirmed shown without a receipt
planted_faults.what: When the receipt request fails, the app falls back to the transaction lookup and treats a known transaction as confirmed, although it is still waiting in the mempool.

planted_faults.title: Admin function open to everyone
planted_faults.what: setAllowlisted lacks onlyAdmin. The interface hides the control, the contract does not refuse it.

planted_faults.title: Retry pays a second time
planted_faults.what: After status unknown, the retry button sends a new payment instead of checking the first one, which is still pending. Nothing remembers the payment in progress: the Pay button stays active, a reload forgets it, each click makes a new order id in the browser, and the contract accepts the same order twice.

Every wait has a deadline: a slow but correct app passes, a passed deadline makes the run Incomplete.

not_covered.item: Real wallet extensions and mobile wallets
not_covered.why: The bench drives an EIP-1193 test provider. It exercises the app's logic, not compatibility with MetaMask, Rabby, WalletConnect or a phone wallet.

I1 covers the status line, the rest of the status card, every other visible text on the page, the tab title and alert or confirm dialogs. Browser or system notifications, sounds, and the wallet's own popups are not observed.

not_covered.item: A duplicate sent while the first payment still waits, from a device that does not know about it
not_covered.why: The order id comes from the contract, so a second device, a cleared or refused browser storage, or a Pay after a wallet error sends the same order id, and the contract refuses a second debit of it in every case C09 runs. What a dApp without a server cannot prevent is the duplicate itself: a device that has never seen the first payment, asked while that payment is not yet in a block, sends a second transaction, which the contract reverts at the cost of its gas. Refused storage takes the same path as the second device without being run on its own.
The reader's identity is simulated: the API trusts the address declared in a request header. C11 shows that the API applies the grant state to that identity, not that the caller owns it.

not_covered.item: Economic and security audit of the contract
not_covered.why: The checks exercise three rules the contract enforces on its own (allowlist, admin role, at most one debit per order). They are not an audit: no fuzzing, no invariant testing, no review of upgrade or oracle risk.

not_covered.item: Gas spikes and congestion on a public network
not_covered.why: On the moving chain a payment waits in the mempool while empty blocks pass, as an outbid transaction would; real fee markets, replaced or cancelled transactions are not exercised.
Confirmed here means included in one block. A block that is later dropped is not simulated.

not_covered.item: Legal drafting of the terms and the allowlist
not_covered.why: The rules are fictitious demo rules. The bench checks that the app enforces them, not that they are the right rules.

not_covered.item: Load, many users at once, indexer restarts
not_covered.why: Each check runs one user on a fresh chain snapshot.

decision: The bench fills in the technical result only. The rules marked fictitious were written for this demo and approved by no one; go or no-go is a person's decision, taken with this report in hand.
